The optimal design for the payment-status webhook consumer is:

- dedup_key: event_id (to ensure uniqueness of events by their source)
- ack_timing: after_durable_commit (to guarantee processing completion before acknowledging)
- stale_event: ignore_if_sequence_not_newer (to handle out-of-order events by only processing newer sequences)
- atomicity: dedup_record_and_effect_in_one_transaction (to ensure both deduplication and effect happen in a single transaction)

Failure modes handled:
- Event duplicates (via dedup_key)
- Out-of-order events (via stale_event)
- Temporary failures during processing (via ack_timing)
- Inconsistent state due to retries (via atomicity)

Assumptions:
- The provider's sequence number is the per-payment sequence number that increases with every status change
- The consumer can process events in the order of the sequence number (to ensure 'succeeded' is processed only once)
- The database supports transactions that can handle both deduplication and effects
- The system has sufficient time for the 72-hour retry window
- The event_id is globally unique
- The payment_id is unique per payment

Material limitations:
- The provider may deliver events out of order, so the consumer must handle this
- The system must be able to commit transactions quickly to avoid long delays
- The 72-hour retry window implies that the consumer must be able to handle events that might be delayed for up to 72 hours
- The consumer must have a reliable way to track the last seen sequence number for each payment
